description: Every configured launch wrapper on the shared manager frame, grouped by type (family), each group with a heading row that names the count and the type's default wrapper (or says there is none) and a plus that adds a wrapper of that type; each wrapper shows its family, the command it runs, the live sessions launched through it and its whole script. Add a wrapper for any family (claude, codex, hermes, openclaw, shell), scoped to whichever family chip is pressed; edit one's label, script, entry, description and model flag; make one the default for its family; and remove one, all from this page (settings-page-move, 2026-09-28 - this used to be split between this page, read only, and Settings, which owned the writes). A wrapper's family and id are fixed once it exists - the id is also a launched session's stored agent type, so moving a wrapper to a different family would change what an already-launched session resolves to; add a new wrapper in the family you want instead. Export saves a wrapper as a small JSON file to share; import checks a shared file, shows its whole script, and writes only after you tick that you read it. An imported wrapper is never made a default. Each wrapper can wear its own icon, chosen with the shared icon picker in its detail pane; the same icon marks it in the new session menu and the restart and wake picker, and its share file carries it. The frame's own actions share it: export in the detail pane saves the file, remove takes away a wrapper that is not a default and that no live session runs through, after asking, and install in the title strip opens the reviewed import.
examples: Send a teammate your claude-chrome wrapper so their sessions launch with the same browser tools.
Check which live sessions still run through an old wrapper before you delete it in settings.
Give claude-chrome a globe so it stands out from your other claude wrappers when you start or restart a session.
